title: Close-up A1+ · Unit 2: Friends & Fun — Vocabulary
subtitle: Clothes, hobbies, personality — build the file on your best friend 🗂️

features.title: What They Wear
features.desc: Sweatshirt, jeans, trainers — the clothes words a description needs before it can start.

features.title: Go, Play or Do
features.desc: The collocation rule: play football · do karate · go swimming. Get it wrong and the English sounds foreign.

features.title: What They're Like
features.desc: Energetic, sporty, sociable, shy, organised — the adjectives that make one friend different from another.

features.title: What They Do Together
features.desc: Chat to, hang out with, meet up, get on with — the verb phrases a real description is built from.

method.phase: Vocab → Reading → Game → Review (Vocabulary of the unit-2 session; the grammar room follows)

games.name: Friend Word Scramble
games.why: production under a clock — the hint is the meaning, so the word is retrieved, not copied

games.name: Adjective & Person Match
games.why: paired recall — the adjective is stored attached to a face and a habit, which is how personality words are actually remembered

games.name: Go, Play or Do Sort
games.why: metacognitive sorting — the learner has to hear the collocation as one word, which is the whole rule

voice: Say it LOUD. Say it WRONG. But SAY IT.
One true sentence about a real friend is worth ten correct sentences about nobody.

storyline: Mai asks the class to write a short file on a friend for the school magazine. Linh describes Mai — clothes, hobbies, personality — and gets one adjective wrong. The group chat votes on the correction, and the class learns that go, play and do are not interchangeable.

rooms.title: The Entrance
rooms.label: Warm-Up
rooms.content:
Two periods, one file 🗂️ By the end you can describe a friend so well that the class knows who it is — clothes, hobbies, personality, and the things you do together.

  • Nine words: clothes, personality adjectives, and two verb phrases
  • The collocation rule: play football · do karate · go swimming
  • The difference between sociable and shy — and why it changes the whole sentence
  • WB pages 11, 12 — you write the file yourself
How this lesson works: every room gives you the words first and the people second. Read every example out loud and swap in a real name from your class — a word you have used about a real person is a word you keep.

rooms.title: The Friend File
rooms.label: Scene
rooms.content:
Mai: For the school magazine, write a short file on one friend. Six lines. No names — we guess who it is 🙋
Linh: Easy. She is sporty and very sociable. She wears a sweatshirt and trainers every day.
Mai: Good. What does she do at the weekend?
Linh: She plays badminton and goes swimming. She does karate too. And she hangs out with us at the park.
Nam: You said sociable. That is not Mai — Mai talks to everybody. This one is shy. She is quiet until she knows you 😅
Linh: You are right. I will write shy and organised instead. One wrong adjective and you described a different person.
🤔 Reality check: the clothes told you what she wears. The verbs told you what she does. Only sociable and shy told you who she is — and that is the part that made Nam recognise her.

rooms.title: The Group Chat
rooms.label: Text Scene
rooms.content:
Linh: ok which one is me: creative, organised, or a complete mess 🧠
Nam: creative. your notebook has glitter in it and no dates
Mai: organised. she colours the timetable. in three colours 🙄
Linh: both then. I am creative AND organised. people can have two
Nam: fine. so what do we do at the weekend — go shopping or hang out at the park?
Linh: we go shopping, then we get on the bus and hang out at the park. we do both 😄
The collocation rule in one line: play + a game or a sport with a ball or a board (play football, play chess) · do + a martial art, a job or schoolwork (do karate, do homework) · go + an activity that ends in -ing (go swimming, go shopping).

rooms.title: The Words
rooms.label: Learn
rooms.content:
1. sweatshirt: a warm, soft top with long sleeves and no buttons — She wears a grey sweatshirt to school.
2. trainers: the soft shoes you wear for sport — also called sneakers — He is wearing new trainers.
3. energetic: full of movement and never tired — Nam is so energetic he runs everywhere.
4. sporty: good at, or always doing, sport — Mai is sporty: badminton, swimming, karate.
5. sociable: happy to talk to everyone, likes being with people — Linh is sociable, she knows the whole school.
6. shy: quiet with people you do not know well — She is shy until you talk to her first.
7. organised: everything in its place, always ready on time — Her timetable is organised in three colours.
8. hang out with: spend relaxed free time with someone — We hang out with our friends at the park.
9. get on with: have a good, easy relationship with someone — I get on with my cousin really well.
Build a file in three lines: clothes + personality + what you do together. He wears a sweatshirt and trainers. He is sporty and sociable. We play badminton and hang out at the park. That is the whole task, done.

rooms.title: Three Friends, Three Files
rooms.label: Reading
rooms.content:
How to use this room: read the file, then the question — the answer is the one line in the file that belongs to that person, not the first name you see.

🗂️ File 1. He is the loudest person in the room. He wears a red sweatshirt and old trainers, and he is energetic — he never sits down. He plays basketball and football, and he does karate on Sundays. Everybody knows him.

🗂️ File 2. She is organised and creative. Her pencil case has everything in it and her drawings are on every wall in the classroom. She goes swimming twice a week, and when she is not drawing she hangs out with two close friends — she is a bit shy with new people.

🗂️ File 3. He is sociable and very sporty. He plays chess, badminton and the guitar, and he gets on with everybody, teachers included. He wears a blue T-shirt and jeans every single day.

Read for the answer: which file describes someone who is shy with new people?
Read for the answer: which file shows the verb do used with a sport?
🤔 Reality check: three files, three people, and not one of them is described by their name. Clothes and hobbies narrow it down; the personality adjective is what actually identifies them — which is why Linh's wrong adjective described a stranger.

rooms.title: Go, Play or Do
rooms.label: Gaps
rooms.content:
How to use this room: the activity tells you the verb. A ball or a board takes play, a martial art or schoolwork takes do, an activity ending in -ing takes go.
Complete the file: She is sporty. She _____ karate on Sundays and swimming on Fridays.
Complete the file: We meet up on Saturdays and we _____ shopping in the market.
The two verb phrases in this lesson: hang out with = relaxed free time together · get on with = a good relationship. I hang out with Nam at the park. I get on with my cousin. Both take with — never forget it.

rooms.title: Game 1 — Friend Scramble
rooms.label: Game 1
rooms.content: How to win: the hint under each row is the meaning — read it, then click the tiles in order. A wrong word shakes and clears itself, so nothing is lost.

rooms.title: Game 2 — Adjective & Habit
rooms.label: Game 2
rooms.content: How to win: click an adjective on the left, then the habit that goes with it on the right. Seven pairs. Wrong pairs shake and let go — guess boldly.

rooms.title: Game 3 — Go, Play or Do
rooms.label: Game 3
rooms.content:
How to win: click a phrase, then the group it belongs to. Say each one out loud as a single word — it should sound like one word, not three.

The three groups: PLAY = a ball game, a board game, an instrument · DO = a martial art, a job, schoolwork · GO = an activity ending in -ing.

rooms.title: The Test
rooms.label: Test
rooms.content:
Scenario: In class she says nothing. In the evening, with two close friends, she talks for hours. Which word describes her?
Scenario: Complete the file: He is sporty. He plays basketball and _____ karate.
Scenario: Which sentence is correct English?

rooms.title: The Key
rooms.label: Mastery
rooms.content:
🎓 You now hold the key
  • Clothes: sweatshirt · shirt · T-shirt · jeans · skirt · trainers · boots · socks.
  • Personality: energetic · sporty · sociable · shy · creative · organised · patient.
  • Collocations: play football / chess / the guitar · do karate / judo / homework · go swimming / shopping / running.
  • Verb phrases: hang out with = relaxed free time · get on with = a good relationship · meet up · chat to.
  • A file is three lines: what they wear, what they are like, what you do together.
Level Up: tonight, describe one real friend out loud in three sentences — clothes, personality, and one thing you do together. Do not say the name. If your family guesses in three tries, your file works.
Write it down (WB pages 11, 12): write your own friend file — six lines, no name. Use two clothes words, two personality adjectives, and one verb phrase with with.
